question.text: If a trader wants to profit from expected increase in commodity volatility without taking a directional view, the best strategy is:

answer.text: Buy both a call and a put option at the same strike (long straddle)
Sell both call and put options

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, a long straddle is constructed by buying a call and a put with the same strike and expiry. It expresses the view that volatility will increase while remaining neutral on direction. The Trap: Buying only a call requires a bullish view. Selling options is hurt by rising volatility. Buying futures requires a directional conviction. Note: The position profits if the underlying moves sharply in either direction by more than the combined premiums paid.
